analyst_view.overall: Both sides have 3 points: Feyenoord are 32nd and Porto 26th, and both need wins to reach the top 24. Feyenoord are six games without a win after Saturday's 3-2 home defeat to Excelsior, leaving Giovanni van Bronckhorst under pressure; top scorer Anis Hadj Moussa (8 goals, 3 assists) came back from Algeria with an ankle problem, sat out Saturday and is still a doubt, and St. Juste, Beelen, Bos, Moder and Nieuwkoop are out (mostly already counted). Porto lead the Portuguese league; Record reports that Farioli has every eligible player fit for the first time in this Champions League, with only Smalling, Vasco Sousa and Gabriel Mec on the medical report. That means the numbers wrongly treat William Gomes as injured and take about 7% off Porto's goals for him. Bosnian referee Irfan Peljto is in charge, and his Champions League games have been low on cards.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.8 goals and take about 7% off Porto because they list William Gomes as injured. Portuguese reports say Porto have every eligible player fit, so that cut should not apply, while Hadj Moussa's doubt pulls Feyenoord's side down a little. Overall I go slightly higher: about 2.9.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.6 corners, with Feyenoord's lower recent count already in (-4.0%). Feyenoord usually have most of the ball at home, and Porto's wide play is unchanged with Gomes available, so I stay at 8.6.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.0 cards and already count both sides' calm recent discipline (-5.9% and -3.9%), but they had no referee to work with. Irfan Peljto averaged only about two to three cards a game in his seven Champions League matches in 2024-25, well below the competition's usual level; a must-win game for two struggling sides could still get scrappy, so I trim only a little, to about 3.8.

shots.text: The numbers say 26.3 shots and already add about 13% to Porto for how many shots Feyenoord have been conceding. Gomes being available adds to Porto's threat while Hadj Moussa's possible absence takes some from Feyenoord, and these roughly cancel out, so I stay at 26.3.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.6 shots on target, including a 12.6% boost for Porto from Feyenoord's poor recent defending and a 4.7% cut for Feyenoord's poor finishing. Gomes's availability and Hadj Moussa's doubt pull in opposite directions, so I stay at 9.6.
